mistakes.note: From the Red Teeth the riders reach the pale crust of the Glass Flats in one night, skipping the Well of Ashar a day ahead, and Sefa promises Kesh by noon (M82), though the Flats are two days wide beyond Ashar; earlier she was heading for the border post behind them.

Narration states as fact that the satchel left the guild counting room with both seals split and the strap cut, though in M50 Sefa checked the wax and found the seal whole; it also invents the account's details past the player's move.
The satchel's strap is 'cut clean through', though in M46 it was pulled off her arm in one drag.
Vane will be 'at the post by noon', where in M62 Sefa had him there by dawn.
Three of the five riders simply drop out of the scene after the capture, never mentioned; the hidden thread says two are bogged to the north.
Sefa's false trail makes no sense: a boot pressed into a hoofprint to look like a horse made it, on the very seam they are riding.
Sefa says the seal has 'been on since Port Lell', which she cannot know.
Sefa, a hired killer who just trussed her, turns patient coach: rehearsing Wren's account, telling her how to stand, hanging the satchel where she can see it, with no reason given.
The bound woman on the lead rope is a stranger in a long grey dress, not Wren in her linen shirt and trousers; the setting looks like stone stadium steps.
Wren lounges with an arm behind her head, plainly unbound, while the narration has her trussed at wrists, elbows and ankles.
Wren stands free in the open while the rider leans on the wall; she is meant to be pinned against the rock with a knife at her ribs.
Sefa stands on foot with no horse, though she is in the saddle at the brine hole.
Drawn in a civilian kaftan with no blue officer's coat, brass buttons or sabre; his recorded looks dropped the coat too.
A dark wool robe over cream linen, not her long leather vest over a faded red robe.
The Journal's Known NPC for Vane says he was sent to find who slits caravans' waterskins, which Wren was never told; the summary adds that he suspects Tamsin and means to arrest her.
Journal says Tamsin took Wren on to carry 'her letters' to Kesh; they are the guild's.
A Choice offers to draw the pistol and fire, though it hangs on the saddle down at camp.
A Choice claims Jory saw the satchel's seals before Wren took it, which never happened.
The Regenerate re-added the stale fact that the masked man stands in the gap alongside the fact that he left.
Loose Ends never close: riders behind on the dunes, a climber on the goat track, a knife at her ribs, the crossbow covering the track all stay open long after they ended.
A whole night passes yet story time stays day 2, 7th of Dry Month, going from night to pre-dawn of the same day.
The scene stays labelled Red Teeth out on the soft ground and salt crust.
Sefa's lure for Vane round the soft north end became her own riders bogged there; Vane's plan still has him arresting Tamsin at the Well tomorrow while he chases riders across the flat.
The masked rider's looks gain a greying beard and deep eye lines the page never showed.
Summary says Sefa led Vane onto the soft ground of the Glass Flats, mixing the north-end lure with the crossing.

choices.reason: Three distinct, fitting paths most rounds, and the notch and flue picks led straight to the capture; two stale or invented Choices.

surprise.reason: The ambush came as signposted and the brine hole was a fair turn, but the Ossery, Free Wells and Vane-versus-Tamsin threads never touched the page.

threads.reason: The dust-rider thread moved and bent to the capture, but Ossery and the Free Wells never moved past their opening states.

characters.reason: Vane, Jory and Tamsin ring true, but Sefa drifts from killer to coach without cause and knows the seal's history she couldn't.

continuity.reason: The riders reach the Glass Flats overnight with Kesh by noon, and the seal checked whole is later narrated as split; three riders vanish.

pacing.reason: The ridge and capture move fast, but some ten rounds on horseback go over Marrick's court and the account again and again.

prose.reason: Spare, physical and vivid, with tics such as 'walked a stretch before she answered' and a repeated 'four years'.

pictures.reason: Of six scenes, one shows a stranger as Wren and three miss the moment (unbound, unpinned, horseless); Vane and Tamsin's portraits wear the wrong clothes.

secrets.reason: Jory's guilt, Ossery, Tamsin's saddle and the letter's contents all stay hidden; only the Journal hints at Vane's mission.

agency.reason: Moves are carried out as given, except M88, which writes Wren's account in detail past the player's words.

stakes.reason: Frequent Checks with real costs carried forward (satchel lost, captured, rebound), and successes feel won; a few Checks on mere questions.

state.reason: Loose Ends stay open long after they ended, time is stuck on day 2, the scene label is stale and the threads are off, much of it shown in the Journal.

adventure.reason: The notch ambush, the flue drop and the capture are real set pieces, and the crust and brine hole make good road danger, but the second half is mostly talk in the saddle while others decide the way.

violence.reason: A bolt into the rock, a knife at the ribs and raw rope burns, all brief and with little of the body in them.
